body: Resistance: Retribution is Bend Studio's PSP third-person shooter, first released in North America on 17 March 2009. It carries the Resistance setting into a campaign designed around the handheld, replacing the console games' first-person view with a camera behind the protagonist. The player confronts the Chimera through a portable action game whose viewpoint makes both the soldier and nearby cover visible. A familiar war becomes readable through another set of controls. The change gives Bend room to build encounters for the machine rather than reproduce a console campaign with fewer inputs.

The third-person camera places the immediate environment around the controlled character, helping the player judge where to stand and how to approach a firing position. Weapons offer different responses to the enemies encountered, encouraging attention to the situation rather than reliance on one repeated attack. The campaign links these encounters into another view of the Resistance conflict. A clear route through a fight depends on recognising what can provide protection and where the next threat is coming from, connecting movement to the use of the equipment currently available.

Christopher Reese and John Garvin directed the project, with Garvin and Jeff Ross writing and Garry Schyman composing its music. Online multiplayer originally supported eight players across modes including team battles, Capture the Flag and Assimilation. The release became the first Resistance developed outside Insomniac Games, adding another studio's handling of the setting. An emulated version reached PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 in 2024. Its original importance lies in that adaptation: a world introduced through console first-person shooting acquires a different camera and structure that suit a separate handheld adventure.
